protocol: B-52H training flight with cabin pressurization failure during ascent. Davis reports 100% oxygen selected at 12,000 ft.
outcome_window: In-flight onset and hospital follow-up. The reports give different accounts of timing at 19,000 ft.
locator: Lewis p. 1263, Table III neurological case 6 and Davis pp. 85–86, Case 1
note: Davis pp. 85–86 Case 1 and Lewis p. 1263 Table III neurological case 6 describe the same 32-year-old bomber gunner with cabin pressurization failure at 19,000 ft, lip and hand paresthesias, visual loss, right hemiparesis and two hyperbaric treatments. Their altitude-to-onset accounts differ. Retain Lewis as the existing case anchor and Davis as the narrative source.

protocol: First chamber training flight of a 27-year-old student. Ascent halted at 25,000 and 28,000 ft. The student was returned to ground through a lock.
outcome_window: In-chamber symptoms, apparent recovery, delayed neurological progression, and return to duty after 20 days of hospitalization.
locator: Printed pp. 86–88, Davis Case 2
note: Source diagnosis. The number of other trainees and their clinical follow-up are unavailable.
